correctness.rationale: For all real alpha>0, Young cutoffs prove compactness; reflection conjugates Jalpha with its adjoint and makes Dalpha sign-antisymmetric. When alpha is noninteger, the kernel columns restricted to x<y split into an ordinary analytic term and an x^alpha analytic term; every nonzero fractional coefficient forces a Vandermonde system of full rank for arbitrarily many columns, so both spectral signs occur infinitely often. For positive integer m the polynomial kernel coefficient matrix is antitriangular of degree 2m-1 with explicitly nonzero antidiagonal, rank 2m, and exactly m eigenvalues per sign. The classical Hilbert-Gram determinant gives the exact nonzero spectral product. The embedded stdlib checker reconstructs exact polynomial kernels and determinants for m=1..6 and 28 fractional Vandermonde test cases; finite checks support, but do not establish, universal claims.

value.rationale: Nonnormality of the classical fractional integral is a standard operator-theoretic problem; the theorem gives a complete natural real-order classification of finite versus infinite signed spectral defects, including an abrupt resonance at every positive integer and a closed nonzero eigenvalue determinant at each integer. This directly quantifies an order-sensitive structural phenomenon, not a routine numeric parameter slice; it also separates compactness from finite-rank nonnormality.
